idea.why: Two independent sources fetched in parallel, one specialist agent per domain, a third editor that only composes and is told to copy stats rather than recompute them. Each agent is pinned to a JSON schema so the renderer has a contract instead of prose. Minor softness: the merge is partly ceremonial and the dashboard exists only as an email body.

structure.why: Fifteen nodes is proportionate and the types are purpose-built throughout: Aggregate rather than Code, structured parsers rather than prompt-and-pray, the HTML node in template mode, Gmail's own filter rather than post-filtering. alwaysOutputData on both aggregates is the right defensive touch. Weak spot: the template carries dense inline map, join and replace expressions.

connections.why: The wiring expresses the real dependency graph rather than a convenient line. Nothing is serialised that did not need to be, there are no decorative edges, and the depth is the honest depth of the work, not padding.

answer.why: End to end this is what the brief asked for, and the template is email-aware with table-cell tiles and no external assets, stripping angle brackets from every agent-written field. Two things a reader would notice: the fetch caps at fifty messages so the total silently understates a busy day, and there is no persistent URL.

appraisal: A well-shaped answer rather than the first shape that compiled: the two fetches genuinely fan out, each domain gets its own agent with a pinned schema, and a separate editor composes the page from those two contracts. The engineering judgment shows in small places, one shared model across three agents, alwaysOutputData so an empty inbox does not stall a branch, explicit empty-state instructions, and angle-bracket stripping before anything enters HTML. What it gets wrong is at the edges: the fifty-message cap means the headline count quietly lies on a heavy day, the Merge does synchronisation the composer's own references already imply, and the template packs loop and escaping logic into expressions that will be unpleasant to edit.
